The first letter is [[alpha]], and the third is [[gamma]]. Anna finds [[kappa]] and [[mu]] on a bus sign. On a café menu, she sees [[theta]] and [[phi]]. [[Chi|chi]] looks like an X, and [[sigma]] looks a bit like E. 'And [[omega]] is the last one!' Max says. Then they climb up to the old [[citadel]] on the hill. Below it, they get lost in a garden [[labyrinth]]. Anna reads the Greek exit sign and finds the way out!

chapters.title: Two Weeks in Tokyo
chapters.story: Max spent two weeks with his friend Kenji in Tokyo. On the first night, they ate [[sushi]] near the station. The next day, they had hot [[ramen]] for lunch. Max bought three [[manga]] books for his little sister. In the park, he saw a woman in a beautiful [[kimono]]. Later, a [[geisha]] walked slowly under the pink [[sakura]] trees. At dinner, Max did not know the table [[etiquette]]. Kenji's [[senpai]] showed him how to hold chopsticks. On the last weekend, a [[typhoon]] hit the city. They stayed inside, played games and laughed all day.

chapters.title: Backpacking in Asia
chapters.story: Anna's friend Lisa went backpacking in Asia last summer and slept in cheap [[hostels|hostel]]. In Seoul, she ate [[kimchi]] with two girls who loved K-pop. When their favorite singer walked on stage, they screamed, "[[Oppa|oppa]]!" In China, she had pork [[bao]] for breakfast and a sweet [[mandarin]] after it. The whole meal cost only twenty [[yuan]]. In Vietnam, she rented a [[moped]] and paid for it in [[dong]]. In Thailand, a market woman sold her fruit for a hundred [[baht]]. Lisa tried [[durian]], but the smell was too strong for her. She liked the [[papaya]] much more. Before her trip, a doctor gave her pills against [[malaria]], just in case. Lisa came home tired, happy, and full of stories.

chapters.title: A Wedding in India
chapters.story: Anna's college friend Priya invited her to a wedding in India. All the women wore bright [[saris|sari]], and Anna wore a borrowed one too. Priya's grandfather wore a white [[dhoti]], and her uncle wore a red [[turban]]. The uncle is a [[Sikh]], and he loves telling old stories. He told Anna about a rich [[raja]] who lived in a golden palace. In the story, a foreign visitor made the servants call him [[sahib]]. After lunch, a snake charmer showed the guests a [[cobra]] in a basket. In the evening, the family went to the temple for a [[puja]]. An old [[mystic]] read prayers in [[Sanskrit]] with his eyes closed. At the end, he gave everyone sweet [[prasad]]. Anna said it was the most beautiful day of her year.

chapters.title: Istanbul, Dubai and Cairo
chapters.story: Max's parents took a long trip around the Middle East this spring. In Istanbul, they went shopping in an old [[bazaar]]. Max's mom paid two hundred [[lira]] for a small blue [[amulet]] for Max. A guide told them about a [[pasha]] who ruled the city long ago. In Dubai, they visited a palace where a [[sheikh]] once welcomed guests. The guide explained that Dubai is the biggest city of its [[emirate]]. On a short stop in Jordan, they paid for a taxi in [[dinars|dinar]]. Then they rode camels across the desert to a green [[oasis]]. On the way, Max's dad saw a lake, but it was only a [[mirage]]. In the morning, a [[scorpion]] was sleeping in his shoe! In Cairo, they heard a [[mullah]] lead the morning prayers at an old mosque. They saw the Great [[Sphinx|sphinx]] and took a boat trip to the Nile [[delta]].

chapters.title: A Safari in Kenya
chapters.story: Anna's aunt Olena always wanted to see wild animals. Her [[travel agent]] found her a cheap [[safari]] in Kenya. Kenya lies right on the [[equator]], so it was hot every day. Olena had never been to the [[tropics]] before. It was her first time on another [[continent]], too. On the first night, she heard a [[hyena]] laughing in the dark. In the morning, a young [[gazelle]] ran past her jeep. The wide [[savanna]] looked golden in the sun. At a village market, she paid fifty [[shillings|shilling]] for a jar of [[shea]] butter. Then she flew to South Africa and changed her money into [[rand]]. She came home with a suntan and a thousand photos.

chapters.title: Max in Latin America
chapters.story: Max traveled to Mexico, where his new friend Diego met him at the bus station. "Welcome, [[amigo]]!" Diego said, and he paid for the taxi with two hundred [[pesos|peso]]. In the evening, Diego's uncles drank [[tequila]] at a small cafe. Max ordered a [[margarita]] without alcohol and watched the sun set behind a tall [[cactus]]. A week later, the two friends flew to Peru. In the mountains, a [[llama]] carried their heavy bags. Their guide said a [[puma]] sometimes walks near this trail. High above them, a huge [[condor]] flew in slow circles. They passed small farms where [[coca]] grows on green hills. In the Amazon jungle, the guide cut a path with a [[machete]]. A [[caiman]] watched them quietly from the river bank. The guide said the river was full of [[piranhas|piranha]], so Max stayed in the boat.

chapters.title: Summer Down Under
chapters.story: Anna's cousin Dan got a summer job at a beach [[resort]] in Australia. On his first day off, he saw a [[kangaroo]] jumping across the road. In a tall tree, a sleepy [[koala]] did not even open its eyes. Near the forest, a wild [[dingo]] watched him and then ran away. A local boy taught Dan how to throw a [[boomerang]]. For dinner, they ate fresh [[crab]] on the beach. Dan slept in a small [[bungalow]] by the sea. One night, a strong [[cyclone]] hit the coast, but his little house stayed safe. On a small island nearby, tourists in bright [[bikinis|bikini]] read a sign: "No [[topless]] sunbathing." A wooden [[tiki]] stood at the door of the beach bar. Far away, red [[lava]] glowed at the top of an old volcano. In the evening, Dan played the [[ukulele]] for his new friends by the fire.

chapters.title: A Week in New York
chapters.story: Anna and Max spent a week in New York in October. Their hotel was [[downtown]], near a wide [[boulevard]]. A huge [[billboard]] over the street showed a smiling cat. On the first evening, they ate dumplings in [[Chinatown]]. On Sunday morning, they went to [[brunch]] at a small cafe. Anna ate a warm [[bagel]] with [[cream cheese]]. Max had a big plate of [[French toast]]. On the way back, Anna found a [[dime]] on the street. "It's lucky money!" she said and laughed. On their last night, they had dinner with Max's cousin Ben. Max ordered a [[steak]], and Anna tried [[lobster]] for the first time. Then they watched the city lights from Ben's [[penthouse]].

chapters.title: Dad's Small Bakery
chapters.story: Last year, Anna's dad decided to become a [[businessman]]. He opened a small bakery with his old friend Taras, who became his [[business partner]]. First, they wrote a [[business plan]], and Anna helped them check the [[cash flow]] every week. After six months, the bakery made its first small [[profit]]. They kept their [[pricing]] simple: every pie cost the same. They chose a local [[vendor]] for flour and sugar. Soon a big [[retailer]] wanted to sell their bread in its stores. Taras had worked in [[retail]] before, so he knew what to say. Then they hired a [[sales manager]] named Iryna. They also joined a farmers' [[cooperative]] to get fresh milk and eggs. Sometimes they even used [[barter]] and paid the farmers with fresh bread. Now a regional [[distributor]] takes their pies to five towns.

chapters.title: Max's Startup
chapters.story: Max and two friends started their own [[startup]] last spring. As the [[founder]], Max had to explain the idea to everyone. The [[concept]] was simple: an app that plans cheap, healthy meals for students. Their [[business model]] was a small monthly payment. Max showed a simple [[use case]]: a tired student opens the app and finds dinner. An [[investor]] named Mrs. Bondar listened carefully. She said the app could be a [[game changer]] for busy students. She offered them a [[win-win]] deal and asked to join their [[venture]]. She put in the [[capital]], and the team brought their [[know-how]]. Soon they got a [[patent]] for their smart shopping list. A local newspaper called Max a young [[innovator]]. His mom cut out the article and put it on the fridge.

chapters.title: Anna's Marketing Seminar
chapters.story: Anna is studying [[marketing]], and on Friday she went to a [[seminar]] at her university. The teacher gave the class a [[case study]] about a small juice company. The company had good juice but very weak [[branding]]. A real [[art director]] helped Anna's team create a new [[logo]] and a [[slogan]]. Then they talked about [[targeting]]: who should buy this juice? Anna's team wanted to sell it to the [[mass market]], not only to rich people. They read a survey, and most [[respondents|respondent]] liked the green bottles. They compared their sales numbers with a [[benchmark]] from a bigger company. Next, they learned about [[merchandising]] and where to put bottles in a store. Anna suggested a summer [[promotion]]: buy two bottles, get one free. Finally, they designed a simple [[landing page]] with the price and a big orange button. The teacher said their project was the best in the class.

chapters.title: A Day at the Tech Expo
chapters.story: Last weekend, Anna helped her friend at a big tech [[expo]] in Kyiv. The [[keynote]] was given by a famous [[businesswoman]] who started as a [[product manager]]. Every [[sponsor]] hung a bright [[banner]] above its stand. At the door, a young [[promoter]] handed Anna a [[flyer]] about a new book. The book, about smart robots, was already a [[bestseller]]. The [[PR]] team sent a [[press release]] to all the news sites at noon. Anna went to a short talk about [[email marketing]] for small shops. The speaker said she had worked in [[high-tech]] for twenty years. The most popular stand had an [[android]] that looked almost human. It smiled, shook Anna's hand and said, "Welcome to the future!" That evening, Anna told Max she wanted a job in [[high tech]] one day.

chapters.title: A Day at the Port
chapters.story: On Saturday, Max visited his uncle Petro at the [[port]] of Odesa. A big ship was waiting in the [[dock]] for repairs. Next to it, an empty oil [[tanker]] carried only seawater as [[ballast]]. "That ship brings oil, and a [[barrel]] costs more every month," his uncle said. In the warehouse, boxes of [[cargo]] moved slowly along a [[conveyor]]. "Grain is our main [[export]], and this coffee is an [[import]] from South America," he explained. "So I am an [[exporter]] and an [[importer]] at the same time." Max asked why the coffee was so expensive. "New [[tariffs|tariff]] on coffee, and each company has a yearly [[quota]] too," Uncle Petro sighed. Then a rich [[industrialist]] in a gray suit arrived at the office. He wanted to start a [[joint venture]] with Max's uncle. That evening, Max told Anna he might study business after all.

chapters.title: Uncle Oleh, the Trader
chapters.story: Anna's uncle Oleh works as a [[trader]] at a big bank in Kyiv. At Sunday lunch, Anna asked him what [[trading]] really is. "I buy and sell shares for people, a bit like a [[broker]]," he said. "You can open your own account at a [[brokerage]] with very little money." He showed her the stock market [[index]] on his phone. "This company pays me a [[dividend]] every quarter," he smiled. Then he admitted that he also bought some [[bitcoin]] last year. "Most people just try to follow the [[smart money]]," he added. He also explained oil [[futures]] and a strange [[derivative]] that nobody at the table understood. His old friend now runs a [[hedge fund]] in London. Anna laughed and said she would study [[asset management]], starting with her pocket money.

chapters.title: Buying a New Flat
chapters.story: Anna's parents finally decided to buy a new flat. A local [[developer]] is building the house, and a [[consortium]] of banks is paying for it. It will be a modern [[condominium]] with a small park and a playground. Anna's mother, who works in [[banking]], quickly found them a good loan. The loan even has a six-month [[grace period]] before the first payment. Their money will stay in [[escrow]] until the flat is ready. The bank, as their [[creditor]], checked how much money they keep in [[reserve]]. The city also gave them a small [[rebate]] for choosing an energy-saving home. Anna's father still worried, so he called his friend, an [[auditor]]. She said the building company had a clean [[audit]] last year. That night, the whole family looked at the plans and chose Anna's future room.

chapters.title: The Economy on TV
chapters.story: Anna and Max were watching the evening news at Max's flat. An [[economist]] in a blue jacket talked about a [[boom]] in online shopping. "But some small shops are close to [[collapse]]," she warned. Then she explained what a budget [[deficit]] is, using a simple chart. "Some countries owe more than a [[trillion]] dollars," she said. Max's grandpa laughed and took an old [[ruble]] coin out of his pocket. "When a country cannot pay its debts, we call it [[default]]," the economist continued. Next, a bank [[insider]] told reporters how a drug [[cartel]] tried to hide its money. Thanks to good [[risk management]], the bank stopped them in time. After that, a [[broker-dealer]] gave tips about buying and selling stocks. Anna yawned and changed the channel to an ad for [[tax-free]] shopping at the airport. "That's the only economy I understand," Max joked.

chapters.title: A Party for the Rich
chapters.story: Max's rich cousin Denys invited him to a [[cocktail party]] in a fancy hotel. The evening started with a funny old-style [[burlesque]] show with songs and jokes. Denys introduced Max to a [[self-made]] businessman from a small village. The man became a [[millionaire]] before he turned thirty. Next to him stood an oil [[magnate]] who owned a huge [[conglomerate]]. "I have [[business interests|business interest]] in five countries," he told Max proudly. A group of actors from [[show business]] were discussing their new movie. "It did great at the [[box office]]," one actress said, eating [[caviar]] on tiny crackers. Later, a quiet old man gave a big [[endowment]] to the university where Max studies. Max decided that was the most impressive thing he saw all night.

chapters.title: Consultants at the Office
chapters.story: On Monday, a [[consultant]] named Laura arrived at Max's company. She works in [[consulting]] and visits a new company every month. She invited everyone to a hall in the [[business center]] for a [[workshop]]. First, she talked about [[project management]] and how to plan tasks better. Then she discussed [[recruiting]] and how to find talented young people. After lunch, she wrote a long [[memorandum]] for the company's [[directorate]]. It also gave advice about working with clients in [[pharma]]. Max helped her put boxes of old papers into the [[shredder]]. The company even sold its old furniture at an [[auction]]. Every [[middle manager]] in the office was worried about their job. But on Friday, Laura said the team was doing great, and everyone finally relaxed.

chapters.title: A Meeting at City Hall
chapters.story: On Tuesday evening, Anna and Max went to a meeting at city hall about their street. On the wall hung a painting of an old [[prefect]] who ruled for an emperor. The [[mayor]] and a local [[alderman]] sat under it and opened the meeting. First, they talked about new [[zoning]] rules and modern [[urban design]]. "We want Kyiv to become a [[smart city]] with apps and sensors," she said. A tired [[bureaucrat]] showed everyone a pile of papers and maps. Then the neighbors got angry. "A [[bulldozer]] will destroy our [[community center]]!" one woman shouted. Others worried about the old [[kiosk]], the [[barbershop]] and the bus [[depot]]. "Some [[squatters|squatter]] live there now, and they need help," an old man added. Finally, the city leaders promised to save the places people loved, and everyone clapped.

chapters.title: Anna Volunteers
chapters.story: This autumn, Anna became a [[volunteer]] at a small [[charity]] in Kyiv. Her boss, Iryna, is a professional [[fundraiser]] with endless energy. Together they do [[fundraising]] for war [[veterans|veteran]] and their families. They also collect money for a little boy with [[lymphoma]]. The charity does [[advocacy]] for old people who live like [[paupers|pauper]] in cold houses. On Saturday, Anna sold forty [[handmade]] cards at the market. After that, she laid flowers at the war [[memorial]] in the park. She thought about the soldiers' [[heroism]] and felt quiet [[patriotism]] in her heart. Then Iryna called with good news: the boy's family now had enough money for treatment.

chapters.title: The New Neighbors
chapters.story: A family of [[immigrants|immigrant]] moved into Anna's building last week. Their son lives in America and just got his [[green card]]. Last month, their daughter Lina visited the [[consulate]], where the [[consul]] helped her. Lina told Anna about [[racism]] at her old school and a [[racist]] neighbor there. Before Kyiv, the family lived in a poor [[ghetto]] in a big, noisy city. Now her parents work hard and hope to join the [[middle class]] here. Anna's grandpa was born in the [[baby boom]], so he is a real [[baby boomer]]. He calls himself a [[nationalist]], so Lina asked him what that means. They had a long but friendly argument about [[nationalism]]. In the end, Grandpa smiled and said, "Every [[migrant]] is welcome at my table."

chapters.title: Election Night Drama
chapters.story: On Sunday night, Anna and Max watched the last episode of their favorite political drama. In the show, a national [[broadcaster]] covers election night in an imaginary country. The old [[president]] and his [[vice president]] wait nervously in their office. Each [[candidate]] gives a speech: a [[democrat]], a [[liberal]] and a [[social democrat]]. They all say they understand the [[electorate]] and want a strong [[mandate]]. Earlier in the season, Max got confused about the [[primaries]] and the [[caucus]]. Anna explained them, and also the [[referendum]] from episode three. A funny British guest, a [[Tory]], keeps comparing everything to London. Outside, a crowd of [[loyalists|loyalist]] waves flags for the old leader. In the end, a young woman with lots of [[charisma]] wins. Max clapped and asked, "Can we watch the next season tomorrow?"

chapters.title: A Day in Parliament
chapters.story: On Thursday, Anna's class went on a school trip to [[parliament]]. A friendly guide explained that every party has its own political [[agenda]]. First, they watched a short press [[briefing]] in a bright hall. A young [[minister]] spoke about new schools, and then the [[premier]] talked about the budget. Mr. Koval explained that some countries have a [[senate]], where each [[senator]] votes on laws. In the hall, a [[lobbyist]] from the energy [[lobby]] waited with a thick folder. The members argued for hours but finally reached a [[compromise]]. The guide said full [[consensus]] is rare, because many people just want the [[status quo]]. Now they had a budget, so there would be no [[shutdown]] this year. Anna asked about [[impeachment]], and Mr. Koval explained it with a funny example. On the bus home, Max asked so many questions that he became the [[de facto]] guide.

chapters.title: A Summit in Geneva
chapters.story: Last week, Anna's aunt Olena worked as an interpreter at a [[summit]] in Geneva. On the first morning, she picked up her badge at the [[secretariat]] on the second floor. The hall was full of [[diplomats|diplomat]] and nervous [[delegates|delegate]] from many countries. Each [[bloc]] wanted to build a stronger [[alliance]] with its neighbors. On the second day, two small countries signed a peace [[pact]]. They also talked about ending an [[embargo]] on fruit and grain. One leader threatened to use his [[veto]], but in the end he agreed. An [[emir]] in white robes gave a short, warm speech. Then the elderly [[sovereign]] of a tiny island kingdom spoke about the ocean. An American [[congressman]] and a [[congresswoman]] from the same state spoke too. Olena translated every word without a single mistake. "Next month, a medical [[congress]] will feel easy," she told Anna that night.

chapters.title: Students protest
chapters.story: On Saturday, Anna and Max joined a student [[protest]] near the university. The city wanted to close the student library and build a parking lot. A young [[activist]] named Sofia spoke first. She said her [[activism]] started in a small library like this one. "We have one [[ideal]]: free books for everyone," she said. Max liked her [[idealism]], but he did not believe in a perfect [[utopia]]. Then workers from a local [[trade union]] arrived with big signs. They called for a [[boycott]] of the new parking company. A man in a black hat said he was an [[anarchist]] and shouted at the sky. Max's friend Oleh, a real [[cynic]], called all the politicians [[hypocrites|hypocrite]]. He said the whole march was [[nonsense]]. Two weeks later, the city kept the library open, and even Oleh brought cake.

chapters.title: A debate about rights
chapters.story: On Friday, Anna's class held a big debate about human rights. First, Anna talked about the history of [[feminism]]. She said her grandmother was the first [[feminist]] she ever knew. Max gave examples of [[sexism]] in sports and in job ads. Then Iryna spoke about [[homophobia]] in schools. She said every [[gay]] student should feel as safe as anyone else. Next, two students shared [[pro-choice]] and [[pro-life]] views and listened to each other politely. The history part was hard: they learned about [[antisemitism]] and [[apartheid]]. They also discussed how an [[extremist]] spreads hate online. In a short film, a young [[skinhead]] left a group of white [[supremacists|supremacist]] forever. The last topic was [[euthanasia]], and nobody agreed at all. Still, their teacher smiled: "You argued, but you respected each other."

chapters.title: Left and right
chapters.story: In politics class, Professor Lysenko drew two big circles on the board. One said [[communism]], and the other said [[capitalism]]. "Between them, you find [[socialism]] and many other ideas," he said. He explained that [[Marxism]] was a theory from the nineteenth century. In that theory, the [[proletariat]] were the workers in the factories. "A [[communist]] wants the state to own almost everything," he said. "A [[socialist]] wants fair taxes and free schools. A [[capitalist]] wants free markets and private business." Max told the class about his great-grandfather, a strong [[anti-communist]]. "But his neighbor called everyone [[comrade]], even the mailman," Max laughed. At the end, the professor wrote one more word: [[liberalism]]. "Next week, we argue about freedom," he said, and the class groaned happily.

chapters.title: Anna's newspaper internship
chapters.story: In July, Anna started a month-long internship in a busy [[newsroom]]. An older [[journalist]] named Petro showed her how to check every fact. Next to him sat a [[columnist]] who was writing the Sunday [[editorial]]. At noon, a [[correspondent]] called from abroad with an [[exclusive]]. She had proof of a big [[scandal]] at a local football club. A [[tabloid]] already had rumors about it. "They want [[publicity]], not facts," Petro said. The [[publisher]] read the morning [[digest]] and asked for a quick [[rewrite]]. He wanted the true story, not the old [[narrative]] about the club. By evening, all the [[media]] were waiting outside the club for a briefing. Petro let Anna write the headline. The next morning, the [[mass media]] everywhere repeated it.

chapters.title: Anna's cousin in the army
chapters.story: Anna's cousin Taras was a [[cadet]] only four years ago. Now he is an [[officer]], and he trains every new [[recruit]]. On Sunday, he visited Anna and told stories over tea. His [[lieutenant]] is strict but fair, and his [[sergeant]] tells terrible jokes. Last month, his [[battalion]] practiced moving a [[convoy]] of trucks through a [[checkpoint]]. They slept one night in a cold [[bunker]] and wore [[camouflage]] in the forest. A small [[drone]] watched them from above, and a [[tank]] moved slowly behind. In the exercise, half of the soldiers played enemy [[combatants|combatant]]. Taras was the colonel's [[adjutant]], so he carried the orders on foot. Anna asked why he chose the army. "I'm a [[patriot]], and I want my family safe," he said. Most of all, they all dream of marching in a big peace [[parade]] together.

chapters.title: Who stole Max's bike?
chapters.story: One morning, Max's bike was gone from the street outside his building. He called the [[cops|cop]], and a young [[detective]] named Koval came an hour later. On the street camera, they saw the [[silhouette]] of a tall man at night. Koval knew him: a local guy with a history of [[shoplifting]] and [[vandalism]]. He had an [[alibi]]: he said he was at his aunt's house all night. The next day, he came back on the [[pretext]] of walking his dog. The police stopped him and found [[ganja]] in his pocket. Koval checked his [[dossier]] and asked for a [[polygraph]] test. Before the test even started, the young [[vandal]] confessed. He and an old soccer [[hooligan]] friend took the bike as a stupid joke. Max got his bike back that evening, with a scratch and a new lock.

chapters.title: A hacker on trial
chapters.story: Anna's law class visited a real courtroom on Tuesday. A young [[hacker]] named Denys sat quietly next to his lawyer. He was on trial for [[hacking]] into a game company and running an email [[scam]]. He also sold [[warez]] on a [[peer-to-peer]] network, against [[copyright]] law. His [[barrister]], an older woman, worked [[pro bono]] because Denys had no money. She talked about an old [[precedent]] and showed an [[affidavit]] from his teacher. Then the [[bailiff]] asked everyone to stand. The [[tribunal]] read its [[verdict]]: guilty, but with a second chance. Now Denys must help a bank find weak spots in its apps. He even has to read every [[disclaimer]] before he clicks "I agree."

chapters.title: A film about gangs
chapters.story: On Friday night, Max watched an old film about the [[mafia]] with his dad. In it, an old [[gangster]] flies to Tokyo to meet the [[yakuza]]. The two groups start a long [[vendetta]] over drug [[trafficking]]. They fight about [[cannabis]] fields and boxes of [[opium]]. Behind them all is a huge crime [[syndicate]]. In the end, a police [[raid]] stops everything in one night. The police find [[bongs|bong]], a [[pistol]], and an old [[shotgun]] in the basement. An expert checks the [[caliber]] of every bullet. Max's dad fell asleep before the end, so Max had to tell him everything.

chapters.title: A true-crime podcast
chapters.story: Anna listens to a true-crime podcast on her way to class. This week, the host talks about a [[maniac]] from an old case. A doctor explains that he was a [[psychopath]], not just a [[sadist]]. He was also a cruel [[abuser]], and his family lived with years of [[abuse]]. Later, he began [[stalking]] young women in his town. The police finally stopped him after a failed [[kidnapping]] with [[chloroform]]. In the second part, an expert explains how to protect children from a [[pedophile]] online. She also explains why [[incest]] and other family crimes often stay hidden. Then a [[coroner]] describes her work in the city [[morgue]]. She laughs and says her hobby is [[cannibalism]] in spiders. Anna takes off her headphones and decides to listen to music tonight.

chapters.title: A thriller about terror
chapters.story: Anna is reading a thriller about the fight against [[terrorism]] in an imaginary country. In the book, a [[terrorist]] group plans an attack on a big port. Its leader is a [[jihadist]], and his men are [[insurgents|insurgent]] from the mountains. They join forces with a [[separatist]] army from the north. Together, they plan [[sabotage]] at the main power station. But the police find a [[detonator]] in an old car. Then they discover a whole [[arsenal]] of weapons on a farm. The [[commandant]] of the base sends soldiers and a young [[medic]]. A navy ship uses [[sonar]] to find the [[aggressors|aggressor]]' small boat. The president arrives at the port with a special [[escort]]. A police [[sniper]] watches the crowd from a roof. The attack never happens, and Anna finally falls asleep at 2 a.m.

chapters.title: Max builds a computer
chapters.story: Max decided to build his own [[desktop]] instead of buying one. He bought new [[hardware]] and spread it all over the kitchen table. First, he read the [[manual]] carefully, page by page. He checked every [[component]] and placed the [[processor]] very gently. He pushed extra memory into each [[slot]], a big [[upgrade]] for games. Then he tested the keyboard [[input]] and the screen [[output]] with a small program. A tiny [[buffer]] error appeared, but he fixed it in five minutes. That evening, his friend Ira brought an old [[prototype]] from her grandfather's garage. Its [[transistors|transistor]] were huge, and it could hold only one [[byte]] at a time. Max laughed: his new computer was a million times faster.

chapters.title: Max learns coding
chapters.story: At Max's company, a [[programmer]] named Lena offered to teach him [[coding]]. On his first day, Max wrote a simple [[test case]] for the login page. A [[tester]] ran it and then read the [[log]] with him. Next, the team started a small [[open source]] project: a friendly help [[bot]]. The bot answers any [[prompt]] about the city's buses. Soon a [[contributor]] from Lviv added a [[plug-in]] for the weather. It uses a free weather [[API]], so the bot knows when it rains. Max asked the bot, "Do I need an umbrella?" It said yes. Next week, the [[beta]] goes to real users, and Max is a little nervous.

chapters.title: Building a Podcast Website
chapters.story: Anna wanted a website for her podcast, so she called Max for help. First, Max bought a [[domain]] with the podcast's name. Then he paid for [[hosting]] on a fast [[web server]]. "I love [[web design]]," he said, "and your old logo needs a [[redesign]] too." He spent two evenings on the [[back end]], and Anna tested the simple [[interface]]. Max checked every [[pixel]] of the new logo in his [[web browser]]. "Why is the video page so slow?" Anna asked. Max explained that [[rendering]] big videos takes time on a small laptop. He also showed her how good [[post-processing]] makes her photos bright and clean. Finally, he added a [[real-time]] chat for her listeners. On Friday, the first fan wrote, "Great new site!"

chapters.title: A Visit to a Data Center
chapters.story: On Monday, Max's team visited a big [[data center]] outside the city. A friendly [[admin]] named Oleh met them at the door. He showed them long rows of machines, and every [[server]] had blinking lights. In the corner stood an old [[mainframe]] that still worked. "We keep popular pages in the [[cache]], so they open fast," Oleh said. "And our [[firewall]] stops strange connections every minute." He showed how each [[batch]] of data travels with the [[Internet Protocol]]. "That's why cloud [[computing]] is so cheap for small companies," he added. On the roof, Max saw a tall radio [[transmitter]]. Back at the office, he played his favorite online game. Thanks to the new connection, his [[ping]] was lower than ever.

chapters.title: Anna Learns Data Science
chapters.story: This fall, Anna started an online [[data science]] course. In the first lesson, she learned how an [[algorithm]] suggests songs to listeners. It finds each [[cluster]] of people with similar taste. "This is [[big data]]," the teacher said, "millions of songs and listeners." For homework, Anna got a small [[dataset]] about coffee shops in Kyiv. She changed one [[parameter]] and watched the results change. In the formula 3x, the [[coefficient]] was three, so the line went up fast. Then she drew a [[vector]] as an arrow on the graph. She colored the background with a soft blue [[gradient]]. Anna noticed a funny [[parallel]] between coffee orders and music taste. When she got bored, she drew a little [[spiral]] in the margin. The best café sat in the upper right [[quadrant]], with cheap coffee and great music.

chapters.title: A Physics Lesson
chapters.story: After the long summer, Taras felt his brain was in [[stasis]]. But his new physics teacher woke everyone up. "Everything around you is made of [[atoms|atom]]," she said. She drew a tiny [[electron]] flying around a [[proton]] and a [[neutron]]. "Light is made of [[photons|photon]], and a [[quark]] is even smaller than a proton," she added. Then she put a ringing phone in a glass jar and pumped out the air. In the [[vacuum]], nobody could hear the phone. "Lightning is a kind of [[plasma]]," she said, pointing at the storm outside. She explained that each nerve sends an electric [[impulse]] to the brain. Then she sang one high note, and a glass on her desk began to shake. "That's [[resonance]]," she laughed. At the end, she gave everyone a [[magnet]], and Taras couldn't wait for more.

chapters.title: The Lemon Battery Project
chapters.story: On Saturday, Max helped Taras with his science project about electricity. First, they read the label on a lamp: sixty [[watts|watt]]. A small battery gave one and a half [[volts|volt]]. "Always check the [[voltage]] before you plug something in," Max said. They measured a resistor, and it had one hundred [[ohms|ohm]]. Taras laughed at a unit called the [[henry]], because it sounded like a person's name. "It's an [[SI]] unit, just like the meter," Max explained. Then they built a lemon battery and pushed an [[electrode]] into each lemon. Max said that each [[ion]] carries a tiny charge through the juice. One electrode was a [[nickel]] coin, and the other was a [[zinc]] nail. Taras read that real phone batteries use [[cobalt]], not lemons. Finally, they read about a nuclear [[reactor]], but Taras still loved their tiny lemon light.

chapters.title: In the Chemistry Lab
chapters.story: Anna's friend Olya worked in a chemistry lab and invited Anna for a tour. First, Olya showed her a tank of [[hydrogen]]. A yellow powder of [[sulfur]] smelled like rotten eggs, and Anna made a face. Above the door, a sign glowed with red [[neon]] light. "Rust is iron [[oxide]]," Olya said, "and table salt is sodium [[chloride]]." She read a shampoo label to Anna: "Free of [[sulfates|sulfate]]." Then she explained that carbon has more than one [[isotope]]. "Plastic is a [[polymer]], and we make new ones here," she said proudly. When Anna cut her finger on a box, Olya cleaned it with [[peroxide]]. "Long ago, doctors used [[ether]] to put patients to sleep," she added. Anna's pencil broke, and Olya joked that its [[graphite]] needed a rest. The best part was a shiny [[chrome]] machine that studied a real [[meteorite]].

chapters.title: Chemistry at Home
chapters.story: On a rainy Sunday, Anna decided to read the labels on things at home. Mom's baking molds were made of [[silicone]], and the cleaning gloves were [[latex]]. The plant fertilizer had [[nitrate]] and [[phosphate]] for strong roots. Her hand gel was mostly [[ethanol]]. In the garage, Dad showed her the antifreeze with [[ethylene glycol]]. "Never use an [[aerosol]] spray near a fire," he warned. In the kitchen, Anna read that carrots are rich in [[beta-carotene]]. Her old paint box said that every color comes from a [[pigment]]. The water bottle listed each [[mineral]], like calcium and magnesium. Dad pointed to the small alarm on the wall that warns about carbon [[monoxide]]. Anna laughed, "The only poison here is the [[cyanide]] in my detective books!"

chapters.title: A Night at the Observatory
chapters.story: On Friday night, Anna and Max visited the city observatory. Through a big [[telescope]], Max saw a bright [[object]] near the moon. "Is it a UFO?" he whispered. "No, it's a small [[asteroid]]," the guide laughed. A minute later, a [[meteor]] crossed the sky, and Anna made a wish. Then a retired [[astronaut]] talked about the beauty of the [[cosmos]]. She explained what scientists think about the [[genesis]] of the universe. She showed a photo of a [[lander]] on Mars next to a deep [[crater]]. "Every second, billions of [[neutrinos|neutrino]] from the sun pass through your body," she said. The guide pointed straight up at the [[zenith]], the highest point of the sky. When Anna asked about the [[zodiac]], the guide smiled. "That's not science, but the stars are still beautiful."

chapters.title: Anna's Psychology Experiment
chapters.story: For her psychology class, Anna ran an [[experiment]]: does music help people study? Noise was one [[factor]], and sleep was another. Honesty was an important [[element]], so she explained every step. Test scores were her main [[indicator]] of success. Max kept losing [[focus]], and his low score hurt his [[ego]] a little. "We can't know that music helps [[a priori]]; we have to test it," Anna said. Half the group got "smart candy" and felt smarter, but it was just the [[placebo effect]]. "What a [[paradox]]: the candy did nothing, but it worked!" Max laughed. In her report, Anna wrote that being "smart" is partly a social [[construct]]. Feelings about the music formed a [[continuum]], from love to hate. Her professor praised her healthy [[skepticism]] and gave her an A.

chapters.title: Genes and Germs
chapters.story: Anna's aunt Lida works at a [[biotech]] lab near the university. One day, she invited Anna to visit. "Here we study the human [[genome]]," she said. She showed a photo of a sheep and said it was a [[clone]]. Under the [[microscope]], Anna saw a [[mutant]] fly with tiny extra wings. Then Lida showed her a [[microbe]] that makes a dangerous [[toxin]]. "This [[enzyme]] breaks the toxin down, and this [[inhibitor]] stops the microbe from growing," she explained. Next, Anna looked at muscle cells and learned that the protein [[actin]] helps them move. "Our team also helps doctors fight [[Ebola]] and [[anthrax]]," Lida said. At home, Anna told Max, "Maybe I'll become a scientist too!"

chapters.title: Brain, Mood and Hormones
chapters.story: On Tuesday, Anna went with her friend Ira to an open lecture at medical school. The professor showed a picture of a [[neuron]], one of billions in the brain. "This outer layer is the [[cortex]]," she said. She explained how each [[receptor]] catches chemicals like [[serotonin]], which affects mood. "An [[antidepressant]] can help when a person feels sad for a long time," she said. Then she talked about [[mania]], when people barely sleep, and [[paranoia]], when they trust no one. A student asked about [[amnesia]], when a person loses memories. The professor said that [[autism]] is simply a different way a brain develops and works. Hormones matter too, like [[testosterone]] and [[estrogen]]. At the end, she tapped Ira's knee, and her leg jumped: a perfect [[reflex]]!

chapters.title: A Week at Medical School
chapters.story: Anna's friend Ira told her about a busy week at medical school. On Monday, her anatomy group studied a [[cadaver]] with great respect. The teacher held up a [[scalpel]] and explained each step. They looked inside the [[abdomen]] and found the small [[appendix]]. Ira also saw the [[pancreas]], which makes insulin, and the huge [[aorta]]. The teacher said the digestive [[tract]] runs from the mouth to the [[anus]]. On Wednesday, Ira watched [[triage]] in the hospital's emergency room. A man with a broken leg had surgery under [[anesthesia]]. Later, a nurse showed Ira how to put in a [[catheter]]. After the long day, Ira felt a sharp [[spasm]] in her back. Still, she called Anna happily: "Today I signed up to be an [[organ]] donor!"

chapters.title: On the hospital ward
chapters.story: On her first day on the hospital ward, Ira met many patients. A young man was happy because his [[tumor]] was not cancer. A brave girl was fighting [[leukemia]], and an old teacher was weak from [[anemia]]. A boy had a rare [[syndrome]], and a little girl showed Ira her [[asthma]] inhaler. A tourist had [[diarrhea]] after drinking tap water, and a painter had [[vertigo]]. At lunch, an old doctor told her stories about [[polio]] and the first [[penicillin]]. Once, he said, a quick [[antidote]] saved a farmer after a snake bite. In one study, some patients felt better after taking only a [[placebo]]. Long ago, [[cholera]] spread through the dirty water of the city. In the evening, Ira helped a family find a quiet [[hospice]] for their grandfather. She went home tired but proud of her work.

chapters.title: A castle in England
chapters.story: Anna visited an old castle in England with Max during the summer holidays. They climbed the stone [[bastion]] and looked at the green fields below. A friendly guide said that a rich [[lord]] built the castle long ago. Later, a [[duke]] lived here, and then an [[earl]] bought it. A [[squire]] owned the village nearby, and each [[yeoman]] farmed his own land. The local [[gentry]] came to big dinners in the great hall. Every [[aristocrat]] wore expensive clothes and danced all night. Once, a [[monarch]] visited the castle and sat on a golden [[throne]]. His [[consort]] stood beside him and smiled at the guests. Their son was too young to rule, so his uncle became [[regent]]. A loyal [[vassal]] promised to protect the boy with his life. At the end, Anna posed like a queen for Max's camera.

chapters.title: Empires of the East
chapters.story: On Tuesday, Taras had a history lesson about great empires of the East. First, the teacher showed a picture of a [[sultan]] in his huge palace. The women of his family lived in a separate part called the [[harem]]. A loyal [[eunuch]] guarded its doors day and night. Next, the class read about a wise [[caliph]] who loved books and science. His [[caliphate]] was bigger than many countries today. Then came a powerful [[khan]] and his army of horse riders. His people were [[nomads|nomad]] who moved their tents across the wide [[steppe]]. Taras laughed at a drawing of a hairy [[yak]] carrying their bags. Finally, a rich [[maharaja]] signed an [[edict]] that opened free schools for poor children. For homework, Taras drew a map of all four empires and got the best mark.

chapters.title: Warriors of the past
chapters.story: Max loves military history, so he spent all Saturday with a thick book. First, he read about a brave [[gladiator]] who fought in a huge arena. A Roman [[centurion]] led a hundred men from his [[legion]] across the hills. In the next chapter, a [[paladin]] defended a small [[fort]] against a big army. Max loved the part where a [[musketeer]] fought a [[duel]] at dawn. Then he read about a [[samurai]] with two swords who served the [[shogun]]. The last story was about a [[commodore]] at sea. His few small ships faced a huge enemy [[armada]]. With a clever [[maneuver]], he hid his ships behind an island and won. In the evening, Max told Anna every story, and she fell asleep on the sofa.

chapters.title: The Wild West
chapters.story: On Friday night, Taras watched an old western with his dad. The first [[colonists|colonist]] arrived by ship and built small towns by the sea. Years later, a family of [[pioneers|pioneer]] traveled west to the [[frontier]]. They got fifty [[acres|acre]] of land near a quiet river. An old [[trapper]] lived alone in the forest and sold them furs. In town, a young [[cowboy]] with a [[revolver]] ordered a [[whiskey]] in the [[saloon]]. Suddenly, news came by [[telegraph]]: [[bandits|bandit]] planned to rob the afternoon train. They had [[dynamite]] and wanted to blow up the bridge. The [[sheriff]] took his big [[magnum]] and rode to the bridge with the cowboy. They got there just before the old [[locomotive]] arrived. The bandits ran away, and the train crossed safely. Taras's dad fell asleep before the end, so Taras told him the story at breakfast.

chapters.title: Dark times
chapters.story: On a rainy Sunday, Anna and Max visited a history museum in Kyiv. The first hall showed portraits of the last [[tsar]] and the German [[kaiser]]. A guide explained how [[imperialism]] made old empires hungry for more land. After the First World War, [[fascism]] grew in several countries in Europe. Old posters showed [[fascists|fascist]] marching in long, straight lines. In Germany, the [[national socialists|national socialist]] made the [[swastika]] their symbol. The quietest room told the story of the [[Holocaust|holocaust]], and many visitors cried there. The guide said that every [[genocide]] starts with hate and silence. In another hall, a [[dictator]] smiled from a poster full of [[propaganda]]. Next to it were letters from a brave [[dissident]] who spent years in prison. The last room showed how people stopped a military [[junta]] with peaceful protests. Outside, Anna held Max's hand and said, "We must remember all of this."

chapters.title: Easter with Grandma
chapters.story: At Easter, Anna went to church with Grandma early in the morning. The [[pastor]] spoke about the [[archangel]] Michael and the coming of the [[messiah]]. After the service, they had tea with Grandma's friend Rosa, a [[Catholic]] from Lviv. Rosa explained that in [[Catholicism]], baptism and marriage are each a [[sacrament]]. She showed them a small [[crucifix]] from her mother. She also explained which old books are part of the Bible's [[canon]]. Her cousin once saw a [[cardinal]] in a red robe at a [[synod]] in Rome. Grandma remembered her own father, who met a kind [[padre]] in the army. The man prayed with the soldiers before every hard day. Later, Rosa invited them to a monastery where an old [[abbot]] makes honey. Anna said yes at once, because she loves honey more than anything.

chapters.title: An evening of many faiths
chapters.story: Anna's college held an evening of many faiths in the big hall. First, a [[Protestant]] student talked about her church choir. A [[Baptist]] from a small town shared his family's Sunday traditions. A friendly [[Mormon]] spoke about helping neighbors, and an old [[Quaker|quaker]] talked about silence and peace. Then a Jewish [[cantor]] sang a beautiful old song. Next, an [[imam]] and another [[cleric]] explained the basics of [[Islam]]. They told the students about fasting during [[Ramadan]] and sharing food with the poor. Pork and alcohol, they said, are [[haram]] for many Muslims. The imam explained that [[jihad]] means struggle, often to be a better person. He added that an [[Islamist]] has political goals, which is different from simply being Muslim. At the end, everyone ate cookies together, and Max ate the most.

chapters.title: A yoga retreat
chapters.story: Anna's friend Lisa went on a yoga [[retreat]] in the mountains for a week. On the first day, a calm [[swami]] taught the group to breathe slowly. A [[brahmin]] from the village told them about the heart [[chakra]]. He also explained [[karma]] and [[dharma]], the idea of duty and right living. Every morning they repeated a [[mantra]], and one man even fell into a [[trance]]. On Wednesday, a [[Buddhist]] teacher came with an old [[lama]]. The old man talked about [[Buddhism]] and read a [[sutra]] in a soft voice. Lisa's favorite [[ritual]] was green tea at sunset with the group. A quiet woman with an [[aura]] of calm became her friend. She taught Lisa about the [[Tao]] and the calm force of [[yin]]. On the last day, Lisa asked her teacher how to reach [[nirvana]]. He smiled and said, "Start by turning off your phone."

chapters.title: Heaven, hell and spirits
chapters.story: After a horror film, Max and Anna argued all the way home. Max is an [[atheist]], and his [[atheism]] makes horror films funny for him. Anna asked him if he believed in [[paradise]] or [[demons|demon]]. "In the film, the [[antichrist]] was just a scary little boy," Max laughed. Anna said the [[exorcism]] scene was the worst part. Max said the [[exorcist]] looked like their math teacher. Then they argued about whether [[armageddon]] would ever come. Max said he does not like any [[dogma]], old or new. Anna called him a little [[inquisitor]] because he asked so many questions. At home, they read about [[voodoo]] and a [[jinn]] in a lamp. Anna's mom, a true [[skeptic]], said, "No more scary stories tonight, please." Then she quietly checked under her own bed.

chapters.title: Grandma's folk tales
chapters.story: On a snowy evening, Grandma told Anna and Max old tales from world [[folklore]]. First came a hungry [[ghoul]] who lived in an old cemetery. Then a [[banshee]] cried in the night, and a tiny [[leprechaun]] hid his gold. Max liked the story of a [[yeti]] who helped lost climbers in the mountains. Anna loved the [[phoenix]] that rose again from its own ashes. Next, Grandma told them about a village [[healer]] who gave a sick boy a [[talisman]]. A [[druid]] in the forest made a magic [[elixir]] from herbs. Far away, a [[shaman]] danced around a tall [[totem]] to call the rain. The people of one tribe prayed to a golden [[idol]] in a cave. A [[charlatan]] tried to sell the villagers fake magic, but nobody bought it. "And where did your old ring come from?" Max asked Grandma. Grandma just smiled, and the ring stayed an [[enigma]].

chapters.title: Hey, mhm, pardon?
chapters.story:
Anna: [[Hey|hey]], Max!
Max: [[Yo|yo]], Anna! What's up?
Anna: Let's go to the cinema tonight.
Max: [[Mhm|mhm]]. Which film?
Anna: [[Hmm|hmm]], maybe the funny one.
Max: [[Pardon|pardon]]? The line is bad.
Anna: The funny film! At six.
Max: [[Okey-dokey|okey-dokey]]. See you at six.
Anna: [[Bye|bye]]!

chapters.title: Wow, Max's New Flat!
chapters.story:
Max: Come in, Anna! This is my new flat.
Anna: [[Wow|wow]]! Look at the view from this window!
Max: Thanks. And this is my new lamp.
Anna: [[Ah|ah]], it looks like a big orange fish. [[Huh|huh]]? Does it really work?
Max: Yes, it does! Now look at my new jacket.
Anna: [[Oho|oho]], very nice! [[Ooh la la|ooh la la]], you look like a movie star!
Max: Now come into the kitchen.
Anna: [[OMG]], what a mess! [[Caramba|caramba]], are those old pizza boxes?
Max: Sorry! But [[voila]], my fridge is full of juice.
Max: Wait, what is under this box? [[Eureka|eureka]]! My lost keys!
Anna: Great! Now let's clean this kitchen together.

chapters.title: Oops! A Bad Morning
chapters.story:
Taras: [[Oops|oops]]! I dropped my phone in the hall.
Mama: Is it OK, Taras?
Taras: Yes, it's fine. [[Brr|brr]], the bathroom is so cold this morning!
Mama: Sorry, the heater is broken. Come and eat your soup.
Taras: [[Feh|feh]], the soup is cold too.
Grandpa: [[Fie|fie]] on this cold house! I sound like an old king in a film.
Anna: [[Boo|boo]]!
Taras: Anna! Don't jump out from behind the door!
Mama: Here, everyone. I made hot pancakes.
Taras: [[Mmm|mmm]], they're so good! Now my morning is better.

chapters.title: Ha-Ha! Movie Night
chapters.story:
Dad: Look, the dog is wearing Grandpa's hat! [[Ha|ha]]!
Dad: And now he's dancing! [[Ha-ha-ha|ha-ha-ha]]!
Anna: [[Heh|heh]], it's a really funny movie.
Taras: [[Ha-ha|ha-ha]]! I'm sending this part to my friends. I wrote "[[hehe]]."
Sofia: [[Hee-hee|hee-hee]]! The dog fell into the cake!
Grandpa: [[Ho-ho|ho-ho]], what do we have here? A dog in a Santa hat!
Grandpa: [[Ho-ho-ho|ho-ho-ho]]! Merry Christmas, little dog!
Mama: Everyone is laughing. This is our best movie night.

chapters.title: Stop! Bravo!
chapters.story:
Max: [[Stop|stop]]! Nobody can go into the castle!
Anna: [[Psst|psst]], Max, you're on the wrong side of the stage.
Teacher: [[Achtung|achtung]], everyone! Just a joke. Now the ship scene, please.
Teacher: [[Basta|basta]]! No more phones on stage.
Taras: [[Mayday|mayday]]! Our plane is falling into the sea!
Anna: We see the plane! Send an [[SOS]] to the coast!
Dad: [[Bravo|bravo]]! What a great show!
Grandma: [[Bravissimo|bravissimo]]! I loved every minute.
Sofia: [[Olé|ole]]! Max, you were the best guard!
Grandpa: [[Vivat|vivat]], young actors!
Max: Thank you! Next time I want to shout "[[banzai]]" like soldiers in old films.

chapters.title: Meow, Moo, Bam!
chapters.story:
Anna: Grandma's village is so quiet. I can finally read my book.
Max: Listen, the kitten says "[[meow]]." It wants food.
Anna: And the cow outside says "[[moo]]."
Grandpa: [[Bam|bam]]! Sorry, the wind closed the door.
Max: Now a car is going "[[beep-beep]]" outside the gate.
Anna: And the old clock in the hall goes "[[tick-tack]]."
Grandma: [[La-la|la-la]]... I forgot the words of my song.
Grandma: [[La-la-la|la-la-la]]... [[Tra-la-la|tra-la-la]]! Dinner is ready!
Anna: This village isn't quiet, Grandma, but I love it.

chapters.title: GG! Game Night
chapters.story:
Taras: Look at my hero's funny new hat!
Dmytro: [[LOL]], it looks like a banana!
Oleh: [[Kek|kek]], that's the best hat in the game.
Dmytro: Why did the robot cross the road? To charge his phone. [[Bazinga|bazinga]]!
Taras: Oh no, the screen says "[[Game over|game over]]."
Oleh: Good match, everyone. [[GG]]!
Mama: Taras, dinner! All this game talk is just [[blah blah blah]] to me.
Taras: OK, Mama, I'm coming!

chapters.title: Ciao! Hello Around the World
chapters.story:
Max: What's in your notebook, Anna?
Anna: Hello and goodbye words from my trips and friends.
Anna: In Italy, people say "[[ciao]]" and "[[arrivederci]]."
Max: And in Mexico?
Anna: "[[Adios|adios]]." My friend from Paris says "[[adieu]]."
Max: What about Hawaii?
Anna: There they say "[[aloha]]." In Japan, I learned "[[konnichiwa]]" and "[[sayonara]]."
Max: And India?
Anna: My yoga teacher says "[[namaste]]." Her mother says "[[namaskar]]."
Max: Cool! Please teach me all of them tomorrow.

chapters.title: Words of Faith and Peace
chapters.story:
Anna: This evening of many faiths is lovely, and everyone greets me so warmly.
Mr. Levin: [[Shalom|shalom]], Anna! Welcome to our evening.
Anna: Thank you! Look, there's Amira, my friend from university.
Amira: [[Salaam|salaam]], Anna! I'm so happy you came.
Anna: Will you come to my birthday party next Saturday?
Amira: [[Inshallah|inshallah]], I'll be there with a cake.
Anna: How is your mother? I heard she was sick.
Amira: [[Alhamdulillah|alhamdulillah]], she's much better now.
Max: Listen, the church choir is starting. They're singing "[[Alleluia|alleluia]]."
Anna: And now the "[[Ave|ave]] Maria." It's so beautiful and calm.
Amira: We use different words, but tonight we all wish each other peace.
